title: Tiramisu
subtitle: Italian coffee cream dessert
excerpt: Savoiardi biscuits soaked in espresso and marsala, layered with a mascarpone cream made from egg yolks and sugar. Sets overnight in the fridge and feeds a crowd from a single dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tiramisu (pick-me-up) is one of the most recognisable Italian desserts. It was created in the Veneto in the 1960s and 1970s, with Il Toula restaurant in Treviso and Le Beccherie in Treviso both among the claimed originators.

recipeTools.notes: A 30 x 20 cm dish for the tiramisu.

content.text: Tiramisu is a layered dessert of espresso-soaked savoiardi biscuits and a mascarpone cream made from egg yolks whisked with sugar and folded through whipped cream. It has to be made ahead: it needs at least four hours in the fridge to set and is even better the next day when the flavours meld and the biscuits soften into the cream.
Mix the cooled espresso with the marsala in a wide, shallow bowl. Whip the double cream to soft peaks in a separate bowl. Set both aside.

Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar in a large bowl for about 5 minutes until the mixture is pale, thick, and falls in a ribbon from the whisk. Beat in the mascarpone until smooth. Fold in the whipped cream.
Dip each savoiardi briefly in the coffee, about 2 seconds per side, just long enough to soak but not disintegrate. Lay in a single layer over the base of the dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the biscuits. Add a second layer of dipped biscuits and top with the remaining cream. Smooth the surface.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. Just before serving, sift a generous layer of cocoa powder over the top.
